service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment in Vail
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats, incentive events and private celebrations at Vail venues, solo through quartet.

faqs.q: How does setup work at a Vail hotel?
faqs.a: Through the dock, on a scheduled window. Vail Village and Lionshead keep cars out of their cores, so hotels receive vendors at loading docks and move gear by freight elevator. We settle the dock time, the elevator window, the route to the floor and where cases wait once the evening starts with the venue in writing before the day. Signet Artists books Vail retreat evenings from Denver.

faqs.q: What power does the band need?
faqs.a: One or two dedicated 20-amp circuits depending on its size, and dedicated means not shared with anything else.

faqs.q: Does the altitude change the performance?
faqs.a: It changes the plan more than the sound. At 8,150 feet singers and horns pace differently in thin, dry air, instruments drift with the temperature swing between sound check and the last set, and we plan a longer sound check. The fee for the music doesn't change.

faqs.q: How loud can it be, indoors and out?
faqs.a: Dinner plays at the level of the conversation, and the closing night plays like a dance band, up to what the venue allows. Outdoors, part of the evening can run on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it. Vail's outdoor cap in the resort villages was reported at 65 dBA, measured ten feet from the permitted area, and the town was reviewing its rules when we checked, so we confirm the current figure with your venue. The cap is a question for the late set more than for dinner.
